issues.detail: The Hebrew 'נְאֻם בִּלְעָם' means 'the oracle/utterance of Balaam', not 'Đức Giê-hô-va phán vậy' (Thus says Yahweh). The Vietnamese adds 'Đức Giê-hô-va' (Yahweh) which is not in the Hebrew text, and misattributes the utterance to Yahweh instead of Balaam.

The Hebrew 'שְׁתֻם הָעָיִן' means 'whose eye is closed/opened' (a reference to Balaam's spiritual sight, often rendered 'whose eyes are opened'), but the Vietnamese 'có mắt sáng tỏ' means 'having clear/bright eyes', which changes the nuance from a specific idiom about opened eyes to a general description of clear sight.
